verdict.rationale: RevenueCat offers a documented MCP server enabling AI assistants to manage subscriptions, products, entitlements, and other billing objects, and a REST API with scoped Secret/Public API keys where sensitive actions like granting promotional entitlements or refunds are gated behind server-side secret keys. However, the story specifically wants agent-driven subscription creation, credit application, and plan changes with fine-grained scoped permissions — evidence shows only broad public/secret key scoping, not granular per-action agent permissions, and no independent/hands-on confirmation of the MCP server actually performing these billing-agent operations end-to-end. missing for 10: granular scoped-permission model for agent actions beyond public/secret key split, hands-on/independent evidence of MCP server executing subscription creation/credit/plan-change flows, and explicit documentation tying MCP server actions to those exact operations.
